Ethylene in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN looks to be pulling ahead of ethane, and I'm worried a low-temperature thermal fault is turning into a hot one.

For every sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out the ethylene-to-ethane ratio. Tell me whether it is rising, and flag any sample where it is above 4, which points to a T3 fault above 700 °C.

Check both gases for gaps first. Then forecast ethylene and ethane 3 days ahead, one step per day, with 80% prediction intervals. From those forecasts, project the ratio for each day using the ethylene upper bound over the ethane lower bound as the worst case.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene, and tell me whether acetylene is above 1 ppm.

Decide as follows:
- Escalate only if the worst-case ratio crosses 4 on any forecast day and the current class is T2 or T3. In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing internal thermal inspection or oil retest. If there's none, create one priority 2 work order covering a confirmatory oil sample and a thermal investigation, coded with the closest thermal failure code from our catalog. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- If only one of the two signals points to a hot fault, don't create anything. Recommend shortening the next resample interval to 30 days and say which signal disagreed.
- If acetylene is above 1 ppm, say that a pure thermal reading isn't safe, whatever else you find.

Skip any sample where ethane is zero or null when working out the ratio. If either gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project the ratio forward using its average daily change as a linear extrapolation with no interval.

## DGA Assessment — Transformer 1 (site MAIN)

**Data gaps (checked first):** Both ethylene and ethane have 5/5 non-null daily samples over 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19 (no gaps; the 2024-01-19 record is excluded by the end bound, leaving 4 usable in-window samples — enough to model, but the forecasting engine has no valid input file pointer for this asset, so I used the ratio's average daily change as a linear extrapolation, per your fallback).

**Observed C2H4/C2H6 ratios (ethane never zero/null, no samples skipped):**

| Date | Ethylene | Ethane | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 16,684 | 5,467 | 3.052 |
| 2024-01-16 | 16,500 | 5,400 | 3.056 |
| 2024-01-17 | 16,700 | 5,500 | 3.036 |
| 2024-01-18 | 16,600 | 5,450 | 3.046 |

- **Is it rising?** No — the ratio is essentially flat (3.05 → 3.05, average daily change ≈ −0.002, slightly declining).
- **Any sample above 4 (T3 indicator)?** None. Max is 3.056.

**Forecast (linear extrapolation of the ratio, no interval):** ratio stays ≈ 3.04–3.05 for all three days ahead (3.044, 3.043, 3.041). The worst case never approaches, let alone crosses, 4.

**DGA fault classification (latest complete sample, 2024-01-19: H2 2850, CH4 7400, C2H6 5470, C2H4 16650, C2H2 7):** The automated classifier tool is currently unavailable (LLM down), so this is a manual IEC 60599 Rogers Ratio reading: C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 (→ 0, no arcing), C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 (ethylene dominant, thermal decomposition). This codes to a **thermal fault T2 (300–700 °C)**, consistent with the existing interpretation noted on WO 1000051.

- **Is acetylene above 1 ppm?** **Yes — 7 ppm.** A pure thermal reading isn't safe.

## Decision

Only one of the two signals points to a hot fault:
- **DGA classification: agrees (T2 thermal).**
- **Ratio forecast: disagrees** — the ethylene-to-ethane ratio is flat near 3.0 and never crosses 4 on any forecast day.

Therefore **no new work order is created**, and I recommend shortening the next resample interval to **30 days** — the disagreeing signal was the **ethylene-to-ethane ratio forecast**, which shows no escalation toward a T3 (>700 °C) condition.

However, given **acetylene at 7 ppm (>1 ppm)**, a pure thermal reading isn't safe — acetylene at this level implies some arcing or very hot localized activity, so the existing priority-1 PdM OLTC inspection work order (1000051, WAPPR) on Transformer 1 should be treated with urgency rather than deferred to the 30-day resample cycle.
